Each student received a copy of the new textbook.
generation: all the people born and living at about the same time
This generation grew up with smartphones and social media.
whether: used to express doubt or choice between alternatives
The useful question is not whether a task is hard, but how it is done.
remain: to continue to exist or stay in the same state
Despite the changes, ticket prices will remain the same next year.
exactly: in a way that is precise or correct in every detail
A fact heard once looks exactly like one that will never be needed.
past: gone by in time; belonging to an earlier time
Over the past year, the company has doubled its workforce.
themselves: used to refer back to the people or things just named as the subject
The children learned to dress themselves before school.
want: to desire or wish for something
A designer fitting the world onto a page may want neither option.
change: A single ingredient can change the whole flavour of a dish.
more: to a greater degree or extent
Careful listeners remember song lyrics more clearly than plain speech.
they: used to refer to people or things already mentioned, as the subject
They arrived late because of heavy traffic on the highway.
voice: the sound produced when speaking or singing; a viewpoint expressed
The rights are real, but the voice speaking for them is borrowed.
moves: A skilled cyclist moves the handlebars only slightly to stay balanced.
community: a group of people living in the same place or sharing something
The whole community gathered to celebrate the festival in the town square.
arenas: large enclosed areas used for sports or entertainment events
đấu trường, địa điểm thi đấu
The city built two new arenas to host international basketball tournaments.
channels: plural of channel; routes or means through which something is transmitted
The bank offers several channels for customers to make payments.
organised: arranged in a systematic or planned way; British spelling
The trip was well organised, with clear schedules for every day.
championships: plural of championship; competitions to determine an overall winner
Athletes from twelve countries competed in the world championships.
sporting: relating to sport or competitive physical activity
The city built a new sporting complex for local athletes.
structures: things that have been built, or ways of arranging parts
Termites build remarkably tall structures out of soil and saliva.
involve: to include or require something as a necessary part
cho tham gia vào, bao gồm
The new job will involve frequent travel to other cities.
carried: transported or supported something while moving
The porter carried the heavy luggage up three flights of stairs.
forward: in the direction that is ahead or onward
The company is moving forward with its expansion plans.
elders: older, respected members of a community
Village elders met to settle the dispute peacefully.
members: people who belong to a group or organisation
The committee has twelve members who meet monthly.
conversations: talks between two or more people
Quiet corners of the café are perfect for private conversations.
representation: something that stands for or depicts something else
The map is only a simplified representation of the coastline.
commercialisation: the process of managing something in a way that focuses on making profit
The commercialisation of the sport brought more money but fewer traditions.
preservation: the act of keeping something safe or in its original state
The preservation of old buildings often depends on funding and community support.
does: performs an action, or auxiliary form used in questions and negatives
She does her best to help everyone around her.
choice: an act of selecting between two or more possibilities
Choosing a university was a difficult choice for her.
between: in the space or time separating two things
The old road runs between two small villages in the valley.
modernity: the quality or condition of being modern
The novel explores the tension between tradition and modernity.
grow: produce or cultivate a plant or crop
Many families grow vegetables in small plots behind their houses.
remaining: still present after the rest has gone or been used
The remaining tickets sold out within minutes of going on sale.
roots: the underground parts of a plant, or the origins of something
The festival keeps the community connected to its cultural roots.
growth: the process of increasing, or a layer that has developed
Algal growth on the pond's surface blocked most of the sunlight.
gave: She gave her old books to the local library.
story: an account of events, real or imagined, told for interest
She wrote a short story about her grandmother's village.
no: not any; used to indicate a complete absence
There was no sound at all in the empty hall.
longer: for a greater length of time
Fresh bread stays soft for longer if wrapped properly.
go: to move or travel from one place to another
We should go before the traffic gets worse.
decide: make a choice or judgment after considering options
The committee will decide next week whether to approve the funding.
